description: Through MOROCCO FARM GUARD, I aim to support climate-resilient crop rotation using NASA data, integrating legal frameworks and digital governance. I’m seeking teammates skilled in AI, Python, GIS, agronomy, remote sensing, or web development to build solutions for Moroccan farmers.
summary:
MOROCCO FARM GUARD is an intelligent agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers, agronomists, and policymakers across Morocco adapt cropping systems to worsening climate volatility and structural drought.

We developed an end-to-end platform powered by authenticated NASA Earth observations (NASA POWER agroclimatology, GPM IMERG precipitation, SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture, and MODIS vegetation indices), coupled with ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 digital soil mapping and 50+ years of official Moroccan agricultural statistics. At its core, the AGROGUARD engine implements the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation to compute daily reference evapotranspiration (𝐸𝑇𝑜) and hydrologic water deficits, alongside a deterministic multi-criteria rotation optimization matrix calibrated with INRA Morocco agronomic research. It features an interactive What-If Climate Stress Simulator, allowing users to stress-test crop rotations against rainfall drops (−10%/−20%) and thermal shifts before sowing.

By translating complex satellite telemetry into localized, parcel-level crop recommendations (e.g., legume integration, drought-tolerant cereals), MOROCCO FARM GUARD bridges the gap between spaceborne data and on-the-ground farming. It safeguards rural livelihoods, conserves depleted groundwater reserves, and bolsters national food sovereignty through transparent, zero-hallucination open science.

Project Details: MOROCCO FARM GUARD (حارس المزارع المغربية)

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data
Platform Version: 2.0.0 (Production / Scientific Edition)

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

MOROCCO FARM GUARD is an intelligent, bilingual/trilingual agricultural decision-support and climate-adaptation platform engineered specifically for Morocco’s diverse agro-ecological basins. It bridges the critical divide between spaceborne Earth observation satellites and real-world farm parcel management.

The platform operates across four fully unified, responsive interfaces:

  1. National Territorial Command Center:
    Provides regional agricultural directorates (ORMVA / DPA) and policymakers with macro-scale drought monitoring across all 12 Moroccan administrative regions. An interactive Leaflet map allows users to click any coordinate in the country or search specific agricultural towns. The system plots real-time dual-axis charts of Daily Hydrological Water Balance—contrasting incoming precipitation (PPP) directly against FAO-56 Penman-Monteith Reference Evapotranspiration (EToET_oETo​)—alongside solar radiation and atmospheric relative humidity.
    • Baseline Strategy: The current monoculture or conventional practice.
    • Legume Diversification Strategy: Strategic inclusion of pulses (faba bean, chickpea, lentil) to naturally fix atmospheric nitrogen and break disease cycles.
    • Drought-Resilient Strategy: Deployment of high-efficiency, water-frugal crops (triticale, drought-tolerant barley, olive, quinoa) optimized for aridification.
    • Precipitation drops (−10% and −20%)
    • Thermal heatwaves (+1∘C and +2∘C)
    • Sowing window shifts (+7 and +15 days autumn onset delay)
      The simulator recomputes the Penman-Monteith energy balance and soil root-zone moisture trajectories in real time, exposing whether a crop will experience stomatal closure, wilting, or yield collapse before the farmer purchases seed.
  2. Evidence & Intelligence Hub & Certified Reports:
    Houses 14,690 official empirical records from the Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture (2010–2022) and 40+ years of multidecadal climate trends (1981–2024) from the High Commission for Planning (HCP). Users can export certified PDF decision dossiers with QR-verifiable data provenance and raw CSV climate time series for offline agronomic field audits.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Water Conservation (25%–35% Reduction in Irrigation Need):
    By synchronizing crop water requirements (ETc) with historical and real-time evaporative demand (ETo​), farmers avoid over-irrigating during low-demand phenological stages and transition away from water-intensive monocultures in depleted water basins.
  • Natural Soil Restoration & Fertilizer Cost Savings (+20% Soil Carbon / Nitrogen):
    Recommends legume integration tailored to the specific clay-loam profile, fixing up to 80–120 kg N/ha naturally and reducing dependence on expensive synthetic chemical nitrogen fertilizers.
  • De-risking Investments Before Planting:
    The What-If simulator allows agricultural credit institutions, insurers, and smallholders to stress-test cropping systems against severe heatwaves and drought scenarios before committing capital.
  • Scientific Transparency (Zero AI Hallucinations):
    Scoring is not generated by an ungrounded black-box LLM. It is calculated by a certified deterministic physical matrix adhering strictly to FAO-56 standards and INRA Morocco research guidelines.
  • Total Inclusivity (Trilingual RTL/LTR Architecture):
    Full native support for Moroccan Arabic (العربية) with automatic right-to-left layout alignment, French (Français), and English, ensuring extension agents, rural youth, and academic researchers work seamlessly in their native language.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Macro-Scale National Water Sovereignty:
    Morocco is facing its sixth consecutive year of structural drought with national dam capacities dropping below 28%. Deploying MOROCCO FARM GUARD provides the Ministry of Agriculture and regional ORMVAs with parcel-level predictive insight to safeguard strategic groundwater aquifers (e.g., Souss, Tadla, Saïss).
  • Smallholder Economic Resilience:
    Over 70% of Morocco's agricultural workforce consists of smallholder farmers vulnerable to climate shocks. By shifting from vulnerable cereal monocultures to diversified pulse-cereal-fodder rotations, smallholder household incomes stabilize even during low-rainfall seasons.
  • Institutional Alignment with National Strategies:
    Directly operationalizes the pillars of Morocco's Génération Green 2020–2030 and Plan Maroc Vert, promoting digital agro-ecological transition and youth agricultural entrepreneurship.

4. What Factors Did Our Team Consider? (Data Trustworthiness & Provenance)

A foundational pillar of our team's engineering design was absolute data trustworthiness and institutional reliability. Recognizing that agricultural advisors, agronomists, and university researchers will only adopt a platform if the underlying data is verifiable and defensible, we integrated data exclusively from world-renowned scientific organizations:

  1. NASA Langley Research Center (NASA POWER):
    Provides continuous 0.5° meteorological reanalysis (MERRA-2 / GEOS-FP) including solar radiation (Rs​), 2m temperatures (Tmin,Tmax), wind speed (u2​), and relative humidity (RH).
  2. NASA GES DISC & CMR (NASA GPM IMERG v07):
    Half-hourly and daily satellite precipitation accumulations at 0.1° (~10 km) resolution, authenticated via official NASA Earthdata Bearer Tokens.
  3. NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (NASA-USDA SMAP L4):
    Hydrological soil wetness assimilation providing surface (0–5 cm) and root-zone (0–100 cm ) volumetric saturation fractions and deficit anomalies.
  4. NASA LP DAAC / AppEEARS (NASA MODIS MOD13Q1):
    250-meter 16-day composite Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) for historical greenness and biomass monitoring.
  5. European Space Agency (Copernicus Sentinel-2):
    10-meter bottom-of-atmosphere surface reflectance for parcel boundary validation and high-resolution vegetation index verification.
  6. ISRIC — World Soil Information (SoilGrids 2.0):
    Global digital soil mapping at 250m resolution combined with local pedological calibration.
  7. INRA Morocco (Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique) & FAO:
    Empirical phenological crop coefficient curves (Kc,ini,Kc,mid,Kc,end) derived from Moroccan field trial stations, ensuring equations reflect local cultivars (durum wheat Karim, barley, faba bean Aguadulce, olive Picholine Marocaine).
  8. Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture & HCP Official Open Data:
    14,690 raw records from regional directorates (DPAs/ORMVAs) and 40+ years of provincial climate time series (data.gov.ma).
  9. Scientific Uncertainty & Spatial Resolution Disclosures:
    The platform explicitly differentiates between gridded satellite reanalysis (10–50 km macro-climate) and in-situ soil tests, providing full transparency so researchers can cite data provenance with confidence.

5. How Is Our Project Creative and Innovative?

  • The What-If Sensitivity Simulator:
    Existing agricultural tools merely display past weather. AGROGUARD dynamically perturbs real NASA satellite time series to simulate future drought shocks, calculating tipping points where specific rotations collapse or thrive.
  • Space-to-Tradition Soil Mapping Engine:
    We innovated an algorithmic bridge connecting continuous machine-learning soil fractions from ISRIC SoilGrids with the traditional Moroccan soil classification system (Tirs, Hamri, Dehs, R'mel, Biyad), making high-tech satellite science instantly intuitive to local Moroccan farmers.
  • Concurrent Aerospace Telemetry Pipeline:
    Using asynchronous Python multiprocessing (ThreadPoolExecutor), the system simultaneously queries five external scientific APIs in parallel, synthesizing satellite climatology, digital soil properties, and vegetation indices for any latitude/longitude in Morocco in under 1.2 seconds.
  • Dual-Tier Aerospace Cockpit Interface:
    A modern, high-contrast UI combining a mission telemetry ribbon, live NASA Earthdata authentication badges, interactive Leaflet parcel selection, and KaTeX-rendered mathematical formulations.

6. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

  • Programming Languages:
    • Python 3.11+ (Backend API, hydrologic modeling, scientific algorithms)
    • TypeScript / JavaScript (Strictly-typed frontend architecture)
    • SQL (Relational schema modeling and analytics)
    • HTML5 / CSS3 / Tailwind CSS (Responsive UI & aerospace design system)
    • FastAPI (Asynchronous, high-performance REST API with automated OpenAPI/Swagger documentation)
    • SQLAlchemy 2.0 (ORM and relational database mapping)
    • Concurrent Futures (ThreadPoolExecutor) (Non-blocking parallel satellite data ingestion)
    • ReportLab (Certified PDF decision dossier compilation with dynamic tables and charts)
    • PyMySQL & Cryptography (Secure database connectivity and password hashing)
    • MySQL 8.0 (Robust relational storage indexing 14,690 official agricultural records, farms, parcels, user authentications, and simulation logs)
    • Next.js 16 (Turbopack Engine) & React 19 (Ultra-fast server/client component rendering)
    • Leaflet & React-Leaflet (Interactive parcel placement, draggable coordinate markers, and Moroccan administrative boundary validation)
    • Recharts (Composed dual-axis time series, evapotranspiration vs. rainfall hydrologic balance charts, and radar score visualizers)
    • Lucide React (Aerospace and agricultural vector iconography)
    • FAO-56 Irrigation and Drainage Paper (Penman-Monteith physical ETo​ model)
    • USDA Soil Textural Triangle Classification
    • INRA Morocco Regional Agronomic Norms
    • Git & GitHub (Version control, automated build validation, and open-source dissemination)
    • Windows 11 Development Environment with PowerShell execution scripts and automated unittest test suites (27 automated tests passing).
